subject: Temporary hiring pause & headcount reallocation — action items for open offers
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Heads-up: CFO requested a temporary hiring pause for Q2 — need a quick triage

Team,

Quick heads-up from finance — CFO has asked for a temporary hiring pause across most non-revenue-facing teams for Q2 while they finish a reforecast. It’s a hard ask to reduce near-term spend; they want a clear list of committed offers and recommended carve-outs within 48 hours.

What I need from you by EOD today:
- List of all active offers / accepted offers where candidates have a signed/soft commitment.
- Recommended disposition for each (honor, delay start, convert to contractor, rescind — only as last resort).
- Any reqs that are mission-critical and should be carved out (with brief justification and expected impact if paused).

Lauren — you have several engineering offers in flight. Priya, can you confirm what we can legally/HR-wise hold vs. withdraw? Marissa, please pull comp band approvals and which offers have manager + comp signoff.

I’d like a short recommendation doc; I’ll take it to CFO and CEO and push for a narrow carve-out where it matters most.

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc:
Date: 2026-03-10T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: CFO requested a temporary hiring pause for Q2 — need a quick triage

Vivek — thanks for the flag.

I pulled our active pipeline and attached an export (offers_in_flight.xlsx) plus the comp band snapshot (comp_bands_Q2.pdf). High level: 7 offers in flight for my org across infra and product teams. 

Short summary (full rows in attachment):
1) SWE-Backend (REQ-1321) — offer accepted, verbal start 2026-04-06, candidate relocated; comp band signoff: yes (manager + total comp). Recommendation: honor start or push to 2026-05-04 latest (candidate is flexible but relocation already paid).
2) SWE-Infra (REQ-1348) — offer accepted, start 2026-04-20; comp signoff: pending (pay band escalation requested). Recommendation: request finance carve-out if possible; otherwise ask candidate to delay to July or convert to contractor for 2 months.
3) Data Engineer (REQ-1310) — offer extended, awaiting response. Recommendation: pause offer acceptance window (extend deadline).
4) PM (REQ-1299) — offer extended, candidate negotiating. Recommendation: pause.
5) SRE (REQ-1287) — strong need (customer-facing reliability work). Recommendation: carve-out if possible.
6) Associate Eng Manager (REQ-1359) — interviewed, not yet offered. Recommendation: pause.
7) Contract SWE (REQ-1303) — contractor, starts next week. Recommendation: proceed but convert several upcoming contractor reqs to extended bench if needed.

Key asks from my side:
- Priya: what are the constraints around delaying start dates vs rescinding? Any legal notice or severance risk if we rescind accepted offers?
- Marissa: please confirm which of these had formal comp committee approval (we flagged two that are pending).

I’ve attached the spreadsheets. I can prepare a 1-page justification for carve-outs (SRE + 1 backend) if finance will consider it.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bennett
Director of Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: CFO requested a temporary hiring pause for Q2 — need a quick triage

Thanks for the quick summary, Lauren. I pulled our commitments and legal constraints — see attached hire_commitments_summary.csv. High-level notes:

- Accepted offers where candidate signed an employment agreement: we are generally expected to honor those; rescinding risks breach of contract exposure and significant reputational impact. Severance exposure varies by jurisdiction; assess per-country.
- Candidates with only verbal acceptance or extended offers: we can extend acceptance deadlines or offer a later start date.
- Relocation payments already issued: we should avoid rescinding; options are to delay start and request repayment arrangements only as a last resort.
- Contractors: easier to pause or not renew.

HR suggestions for near-term actions:
1) Honor signed offers unless finance explicitly directs rescind — instead, request a start-date deferral and provide a clear timeline/communication.
2) For offers with pending comp committee approval: put on hold immediately.
3) For offers in negotiation: freeze and extend deadlines.
4) For mission-critical roles (SRE + one backend): ask Vivek/Finance for a formal carve-out memo; we can prioritize those in the approval queue.

I can draft candidate communications templates for delayed starts and for extending offer deadlines. If you want to follow up with a legal review for the handful of signed agreements, loop in legal and I’ll schedule a priority consult.

—
Priya Natarajan
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: CEO <ceo@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask: decision on 3 active offers in Platform org — need carve-out guidance

Hi —

Following Vivek’s note and Priya’s guidance, I’m requesting an expedited decision on three active offers in Platform that materially affect our roadmap:
- REQ-1321 SWE-Backend (signed offer, relocation paid) — recommend honor or allow a 4-week deferral; high customer impact if delayed.
- REQ-1348 SWE-Infra (signed offer, comp escalation pending) — prefer carve-out; alternative is contractor conversion.
- REQ-1287 SRE (offer accepted verbally; critical for SLAs) — prefer carve-out.

If we can carve out two headcounts (one SRE, one backend), I’ll reprioritize and reallocate the remainder of my open reqs and freeze all non-critical hiring. I’ve attached the spreadsheet summary and the comp band snapshot for context.

Related link: https://redwood.company.drive/Headcount/2026Q2-HC-Plan

Happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Lauren

--
Lauren Bennett
Director of Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Finance Ops <finance.ops@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: decision on 3 active offers in Platform org — need carve-out guidance

Team,

Thanks for the fast turn-around. CFO and CEO have approved a very narrow carve-out: we will approve two exceptions for Platform this quarter — specifically: REQ-1321 (SWE-Backend) and REQ-1287 (SRE). The rest of Platform’s open reqs must be paused immediately. Finance will not approve additional headcount until the reforecast is complete.

Action items:
- Lauren: proceed to finalize onboarding logistics for REQ-1321 and REQ-1287; coordinate with Priya on start-date confirmation and relocation payments.
- Priya: prepare candidate communications for the 4 offers we are placing on hold (templates for delayed start + deadline extensions).
- Marissa/Finance Ops: reassign two backend headcount slots to Infrastructure/SRE pool in the headcount tracker and update the HC plan (link above). Please confirm req numbers updated (REQ-1321 and REQ-1287 remain active; mark others paused).
- Legal: standby for one-off review if any signed-agreement edge cases arise (Priya will escalate).

We’ll reconvene after the reforecast to revisit. Lauren — thanks for prioritizing the justification.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Strategy
Redwood Inference
